title: 四十个黄柠檬  (Forty Yellow Lemons)

segments.t: Friday morning dawns bright and clear at Courtyard Inn—grand opening day for Room Nine's garden café! In the kitchen, Mei stands happily at her counter without pillows while Qing and Peng roll up their sleeves over bowls of yellow lemons. Listen first.
小美！你看你，两只脚稳稳站在炉子前了！
垫着枕头歇了两天真管用——今天一点也不疼了！
那太好了，大厨，我们刚从集市买回四十个新鲜柠檬。
四十个柠檬，正好烤四大盘六点钟的杏仁柠檬挞！
小美，你觉得今晚真会有多少邻居来呀？
有免费音乐和热面包，消息在梧桐巷传得可快了！
我已经切了十个柠檬；小晴正在打鸡蛋和白糖。
小晴，你先看清糖罐上的大红标签了吗？
看了两遍，还尝了一小撮！像夏天一样甜！
小美，二十四杯热茶一起上，够喝吗？
两大壶红茶、两壶院子里的新鲜薄荷茶，还有热牛奶。
第一盘进烤箱啦——六点钟，我们准备好啦！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
小美！你看你，两只脚稳稳站在炉子前了！

'Mei! Look at you standing steady at the stove on both feet!' Repeating "wen" as "wenwen" turns "steady" into a vivid picture of Mei planted firmly on both feet. Mandarin loves doubling descriptive words like this to make a moment feel warm and immediate.
垫着枕头歇了两天真管用——今天一点也不疼了！

'Resting two days on those pillows worked wonders—not a single twinge today!' Mei's everyday word "guanyong" literally joins "manage" and "use"—the natural spoken way to say a remedy really works. At the end, "yidian ye bu" means "not even a tiny bit".
那太好了，大厨，我们刚从集市买回四十个新鲜柠檬。

'Good thing too, chef, because we just brought back forty fresh lemons from the market.' Peng affectionately calls Mei "dachu", literally "big kitchen", the warm everyday title for a head cook. Notice how "ge" sits between "forty" and "fresh lemons" to count the fruit.
四十个柠檬，正好烤四大盘六点钟的杏仁柠檬挞！

'Forty lemons works out right to bake four big trays of almond lemon tart for six o'clock!' "Zhenghao" joins "exact" and "good" to mean "just right". And for flat baking trays, Mandarin counts with "pan", the same word used for plates and serving dishes.
小美，你觉得今晚真会有多少邻居来呀？

'How many neighbours do you think will actually come tonight, Mei?' Instead of flipping word order for a question, Qing keeps statement order and drops "duoshao"—literally "many-few"—right where the number belongs. Soft "ya" at the end warms her voice.
有免费音乐和热面包，消息在梧桐巷传得可快了！

'When free music and warm bread meet, word travels mighty fast on Wutong Lane!' "Mianfei" literally means "exempt from fee"—"free". Around "fast", the lively frame "ke... le" gives Mei's prediction extra sparkle.
我已经切了十个柠檬；小晴正在打鸡蛋和白糖。

'I already sliced ten lemons; Qing is beating the eggs and white sugar.' One hardworking word, "da", covers phoning, playing ball, and here whisking eggs. Putting "zhengzai" right in front shows she is right in the middle of doing it.
小晴，你先看清糖罐上的大红标签了吗？

'Did you check the big red label on the sugar jar clearly first, Qing?' Mei glues "kan", "look", to "qing", "clear", building "kanqing"—to look and make sure you read it clearly—after Tuesday night's mystery-jar scare.
看了两遍，还尝了一小撮！像夏天一样甜！

'Checked twice and tasted a pinch! Sweet as summer!' "Liang bian" counts checking the whole label through twice from start to finish. And Mandarin builds "sweet as summer" with "xiang... yiyang tian", literally "resembling summer same-sweet".
小美，二十四杯热茶一起上，够喝吗？

'What about serving twenty-four cups of hot tea all at once, Mei—will there be enough?' "Yiqi shang" packs "serve them all together" into three brisk syllables you will hear in every Chinese restaurant and teahouse.
两大壶红茶、两壶院子里的新鲜薄荷茶，还有热牛奶。

'Two big pots of black tea, two pots of fresh courtyard mint tea, and hot milk.' Watch out for a classic surprise: what English calls "black tea" is "hongcha" in Mandarin, literally "red tea", named after the warm coppery colour in the cup rather than the dry leaves.
第一盘进烤箱啦——六点钟，我们准备好啦！
'Into the oven goes tray number one—six o'clock, we are ready!' Putting "di" before "one" turns "one tray" into "tray number one", and "kaoxiang" literally means "bake-box"—the kitchen oven.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
小美！你看你，两只脚稳稳站在炉子前了！
垫着枕头歇了两天真管用——今天一点也不疼了！
那太好了，大厨，我们刚从集市买回四十个新鲜柠檬。
四十个柠檬，正好烤四大盘六点钟的杏仁柠檬挞！
小美，你觉得今晚真会有多少邻居来呀？
有免费音乐和热面包，消息在梧桐巷传得可快了！
我已经切了十个柠檬；小晴正在打鸡蛋和白糖。
小晴，你先看清糖罐上的大红标签了吗？
看了两遍，还尝了一小撮！像夏天一样甜！
小美，二十四杯热茶一起上，够喝吗？
两大壶红茶、两壶院子里的新鲜薄荷茶，还有热牛奶。
第一盘进烤箱啦——六点钟，我们准备好啦！
Mei is back on her feet, the sugar jar is verified twice, and forty lemons are turning into golden tarts for tonight. See you next time.
回头见！
